previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, hypertension, GERD, and recurrent DVT/PE on warfarin presented with three days of diffuse abdominal pain, diarrhea, and dysuria. She was found to have hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and a urinary tract infection. Imaging showed diverticulosis without diverticulitis and bibasilar atelectasis likely due to splinting from abdominal pain. She was treated with IV fluids, potassium repletion, and antibiotics, initially for presumed viral gastroenteritis and confirmed UTI. Her symptoms improved rapidly, potassium normalized, and she tolerated a regular diet. Warfarin was reduced to 1 mg daily due to antibiotic interaction, and furosemide was held. She was discharged home in stable condition with a three-day course of oral ciprofloxacin, instructions to follow up on INR and medication management, and advised to monitor for weight gain or worsening symptoms.

*** Active Diagnoses ***

#Abdominal Pain ___ Constipation:
Work-up performed that showed no concerning masses or lesions on 
CT scan. No concerns for acute obstruction and normal LFTs and 
lipase. Given history and age likely functional chronic 
constipation although secondary causes including chronic changes 
from diverticulosis ___ Colonoscopy), anorectal anatomic 
defects and diet including the use of iron supplements may have 
been contributing. Iron supplements held during admission 
(normal Ferritin and evidence of macrocytic anemia). For 
treatment of constipation, patient was given warm water enema 
with senna and colace with +bm that led to near resolution of 
her abdominal pain. Initially, pt experienced episodes of 
diarrhea with stool cultures/C.diff/ova+parasites collected and 
found to be negative. Although diarrhea resolved prior to 
discharge, prescriptions for bowel regimen were held upon 
discharge in light of diarrheal episode and risk of patient 
become hypokalemic (see below) until being re-assessed by Dr. 
___ at the appointment arranged. 

#Chronic PE/DVT: 
Coumadin dose halved on last admission in setting of 
ciprofloxacin. Her INR subtherapeutic during admission with a 
heparin bridge started as coumadin adjusted to achieve goal INR. 
The patient was switched to a Lovenox bridge for possible 
discharge, but was found that patient had only 1 episode of 
bilateral DVT with PE in the past such that patient did not 
necessarily need bridging therapy and not received bridges 
during prior admissions. Patient arranged for follow-up at 
___ upon discharge.

#Hyponatremia/hypokalemia: 
Likely due to poor PO intake and vomitting prior to admission. 
Repleted during hospital admission with normal sodium and 
potassium obtained. Initially after constipation resolved, pt 
experienced mild diarrhea leading to low K that stabilized 
shortly after diarrhea had subsided. Encourage adequate PO 
intake.

# Urinary incontinence/decreased urine output: 
Likely due to hypovolemia. Could be due to obstructive component 
given enlarged bladder on CT scan, but PVRs unremarkable with 
patient showing evidence of good UOP on date of discharge withou 
evidence of retention. UA was negative

# Chronic anemia:
In the past had been a microcytic anemia that responded to iron 
supplementation. Her recent ferritin was wnl of 67. Recently, 
including her present admission, her anemia has predominantly 
been macrocytic. Vitamin B12 and Folate levels checked that 
showed normal B12 and folate levels. At this time hold the iron 
given issues with constipation (above). Anemia may be due to 
gastritis.

#Chronic compensated heart failure:
Stable during admission, continued metoprolol. No evidence of

Discharge Instructions:
Hello Ms. ___,

You came in with abdominal pain due likely to constipation. This 
may be related to starting iron supplements. CT scan (X-ray of 
your stomach) showed no new findings including no evidence of 
significant blockage. After you had bowel movements, your pain 
improved but started having episode of diarrhea that we checked 
for infection such as C. Diff (a bacteria common after taking 
antibiotics) that you did not have. Your diarrhea eventually 
resolved prior to discharge. At your follow-up appointment 
please discuss whether or not you would benefit from standing 
stool softeners. 

Your potassium was also low which we believe was due to your 
diarrhea. We gave you medication to increase your potassium 
(nutrient in your blood). Other results are pending that your 
primary care physician, ___ be able to follow-up.

Please TAKE the prescribed NEW medications for your abdominal 
pain:
- Simethicone 80mg: Take 1 tablet four times a day as needed for 
bloating or gas.

You may also consider drinking prune juice as a way to reduce 
constipation.

Please STOP taking the following medications:

- Iron supplements because it may be making your constipation 
worse.

If you experience significantly worsened pain despite treatment 
or any fevers, chills, nausea, or vomiting then please contact 
your primary care physician or come to the emergency room.

Please follow-up with your primary care physician ___ 
___ weeks (see appointment below). Please continue to follow-up 
at the Coumadin (Wafarin) clinic to help adjust your blood 
thinning medications.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Central umbilical pain with severe tenderness.  Evaluate for
acute process.

COMPARISONS:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis from ___.  CT of the
abdomen and pelvis from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis after the administration of IV contrast only.  Sagittal and coronal
reformatted images were obtained and reviewed.

FINDINGS:

LUNG BASES:  There is minimal bibasilar atelectasis.  The bases of the lungs
are otherwise clear.  There is a small left pleural lipoma, which is unchanged
from the prior exam.  The heart size is normal.  There is no pericardial
effusion.

ABDOMEN:  The liver is normal in shape and contour.  There are no focal
hepatic lesions.  The portal vein is patent.  There is no intra- or
extra-hepatic biliary duct dilation.  The gallbladder, spleen, pancreas, and
adrenal glands are normal.  A small hypodensity in the left kidney is too
small to fully characterize and measures 7 mm (2, 29).  It is unchanged from
the prior exam, and statistically represents a cyst.  The kidneys are
otherwise normal.  There is no hydronephrosis.  The kidneys enhance and
excrete contrast symmetrically.

The stomach and small bowel are normal in course and caliber.  There is no
evidence of obstruction.  There is no free air or free fluid.  There is no
mesenteric, abdominal, or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.  The abdominal
vasculature is normal in course and caliber.  Mild atherosclerotic disease is
noted along its course.

PELVIS:  There is extensive diverticulosis without evidence of diverticulitis.
The appendix is normal.  The bladder is normal.  The uterus is atrophic. 
There are no adnexal lesions.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.  There is
no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  The patient is status post a total left hip arthroplasty.
No fractures identified.  Mild multilevel degenerative changes are noted in
the lower lumbar and lower thoracic spine.

IMPRESSION:  Extensive diverticulosis without evidence of diverticulitis.  No
acute abdominal pathology to explain the patient's pain.
